proposal.observation: Round-1 overlay (binary_threshold 115, hough_oblique 30, maxLineGap 45) was accepted: correspondence_f1@15 0.172 -> 0.184, boundary_explained_edge@25 0.209 -> 0.247, chamfer 96.3 -> 95.2 px, while sam_fill_rate, ring_count_error and depth_nan_ratio were unchanged. However the before/after detected_lines.png are visually indistinguishable: still 3 positive (green) and 2-3 negative (red) oblique segments, all in the right-most three rings (x~1690-2450), one horizontal fallback line, and initial_prompt_points.png still shows all 10 prompt centres 'propagated' at one y~1550. Pixel measurement of the drawn lines (image aspect preserved, ~2.28 data px per image px) gives green slopes of +5.2/+5.8/+5.9 deg and the clean red segment -4.7 deg, i.e. a taper of ~5-6 deg, and a K block that spans y~1485 (top edge) to y~1662 (bottom edge) at ring centre, i.e. ~177 px ~ 885 mm at 5 mm/px with centre y~1573 (the propagated prompts sit ~23 px above this). One red segment spans x 937-1145 image px (two rings) with a fitted slope of only -1.7 deg: with maxLineGap=45 the Hough is bridging the ~45 data px gap between the joint marks of adjacent rings, producing a merged, flattened segment that falls outside the [-10,-5] angle window. Joint marks remain visible in all ten ring columns of the outlier map but are smaller/sparser on the left seven rings.
proposal.rule: d7 (stage_4_detection): m_line_yield low AND horizontal fallback triggered -> f_missing_lines (persisting after a mild relaxation), with a secondary d8/d10 signal: the template K block geometry (K_height, taper angle) should be set from the observed joint lines so the SAM template boundaries land within the 15 px correspondence window (r_fix_template / r_fix_height_priors). Remediations: r_relax_hough (lower oblique threshold further, lower binarisation threshold) but with maxLineGap reduced so segments are not bridged across ring boundaries; r_fix_template (K_height, angle from measured lines).
proposal.rationale: Round 1 confirmed the direction (accepted, +0.007 proxy) but the step was too small to convert the left-side joint marks into lines, so the K locus is still propagated from a single ring. This round pushes the oblique Hough accumulator threshold to 22 and the binarisation threshold to 105 so the sparser left-side marks accumulate enough votes, while REDUCING maxLineGap_oblique from 45 to 30 so a segment cannot bridge the ~45 px inter-ring gap (which currently produces a flattened cross-ring segment that fails the angle filter). Vertical Hough threshold, pattern_tolerance and uniform_k_snap are untouched because the 10 ring boundaries are exact and a single shared K height is correct for the continuous family. In the SAM stage, K_height=885 mm and angle=5.5 deg are set directly from the measured line geometry (177 px K span, 5-6 deg taper); both are near the middle of their bounds, so if the incumbent already matches, the template is unchanged, and otherwise the K/B block edges move toward the observed joint lines, which is what correspondence_f1@15 and boundary_explained_edge measure. Denoising/enhancing are untouched (depth_nan_ratio and fill rate healthy); unfolding untouched (stage 1 locked). Worked example g005 (hough_oblique 22 together with binary_threshold 150, vertical 822, pattern_tolerance 19, snap on) collapsed f1 as a joint outcome; here the low oblique threshold is paired with a LOWER binary threshold and no vertical/pattern changes, so that regime is not reproduced.
